static_traits.name: Lin Wei
static_traits.family_status: Lives with parents and one sibling
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive group of sports-fan friends, but has not yet discussed with them how game results affect her mood; relationships with friends who do not share the team passion are somewhat tense
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy received in the past; no history of similar psychological problems yet reported
static_traits.language_features: Expression is clear and logicality relatively good, willing to try reality testing; tone is neutral; when talking about the team losing, tendencies to 'absolutization/black-and-white', overgeneralization and prophetic thinking appear

basic_info.main_problem: Whenever my favorite team, the Raptors, loses, I feel strong disappointment and sadness, and thus believe they will never win a championship.
basic_info.core_demands: After realizing that his strong emotional reactions to the team's performance significantly affect daily life and overall mood, hopes to reduce these effects through counseling.
growth_experiences: Since becoming a Raptors fan in adolescence, her emotional reactions have fluctuated with game results: stress rises markedly after important games or losses; the problem has worsened over time, with post-game low mood lasting longer, forming a hopeless pattern about the team's future success (losing one game means 'never winning a championship'); emotional distress affects sleep and enjoyment of activities, and creates tension in relationships with friends who are not enthusiastic.

core_beliefs: Only winning a championship counts as 'good enough/successful'; failure means hopelessness

special_situations.event: The Raptors lose in the regular season or a key game
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the team has not won a championship, it means they are not good enough and will not succeed in the future either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries distraction (focusing on study, spending time with family) to relieve disappointment and sadness
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will never win a championship / never be good enough

special_situations.event: When important games go against the Raptors or just after a loss
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once unfavorable signs appear, the outcome is inevitably failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Lowering expectations, avoiding discussing competition performance with others to reduce embarrassment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They always fail at crucial moments and will keep losing in the future

special_situations.event: When reviewing the team's performance after a game, recent losses dominate attention
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Recent results best reflect overall strength; past successes are meaningless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to stop negative thinking with distraction, but it often does not work
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The previous good seasons and that championship were all undone by recent losses

special_situations.event: After every game loss, mood drops markedly and lasts for days
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One failure equals long-term failure, meaning no hope for the future
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly thinks about the defeat in an attempt to 'be mentally prepared'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Losing one game proves they will never win a championship later

core_conflict.wish: Longs to gain a sense of certainty and meaning through the team's continued victories and championships, and emotions are soothed
core_conflict.fear: Fearing experiencing disappointment and hopelessness again, worrying that emotional loss of control will affect daily life and interpersonal relationships
defense_goal: Reduces injury and embarrassment by lowering expectations and avoiding discussion
Preemptively warding off future disappointment with the conclusion 'they will never win a championship'

object_relations.self_representation: An invested and vulnerable loyal fan, easily struck by losses
object_relations.object_representation: An uncontrollable, often disappointing external object (the team/games)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites examining game performance from different angles and reality-testing
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client tends to believe 'the evidence is that they keep losing', and is skeptical of a balanced perspective (transference: overlaying the current conversation with past experiences of defeat)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: When responding, first affirm their feelings, then gently point out the selectivity of the evidence, provide specific data for comparison; tone is steady, avoid confrontation, use inviting questions to encourage them to list facts on both the positive and negative sides at the same time.

manifestations: After a team loss, developing strong disappointment and hopelessness, believing future success is unattainable
Positive experiences are overshadowed by recent defeats, making it hard to feel meaning and value
outcomes: Low mood and sadness lasting for days

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Feeling embarrassed to discuss team emotions with friends, choosing not to speak
Turning the need for outward expression and help-seeking against the self, trying to digest emotions alone through distraction

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: After losing a competition, avoids directly contacting disappointment through distraction and other hobbies
When talking about positive moments, easily turning back to focusing on recent losses

positive_force: Willing to try reality testing and restructuring thoughts, and showing cooperation and openness in counseling
Has a supportive group of sports-fan friends
Academics not yet significantly affected, with some self-management capacity
Able to identify and name her own negative automatic thoughts
negative_force: Strong tendency toward overgeneralization and 'predicting the future', easily reaching hopeless conclusions
Post-game negative focus dominates, tending to negate positive experiences
Avoiding communication when meeting interpersonal misunderstanding, leading to relationship tension
Emotional distress affects sleep and enjoyment of activities

target_behavior.behavior: Strong disappointment and sadness after team losses, with hopeless thinking
antecedent: Important games or unfavorable game trends
target_behavior.core_reason: Using 'championship = good enough/successful' as the sole standard, catastrophically inferring future failure from recent losses
target_behavior.function: Avoiding uncertainty and further disappointment by presetting the worst outcome (emotional avoidance)
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood lasting for days, affecting sleep and enjoyment of activities

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding discussing games and emotions with friends who do not share the team passion
antecedent: When interacting with friends who are not enthusiastic
Being asked about team performance after the match
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying that communicating will be awkward and not understood
target_behavior.function: Escaping unwelcome social feedback, reducing conflict and shame
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal relationships become tense, with less communication
